rules.title: Use and sale of coordinated pricing algorithms prohibited
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or provide coordinated pricing algorithms to landlords, or for landlords to use such algorithms to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.exemptions: Products or processes that generate aggregated and anonymous rental data reports without recommending rent prices or fees, products used to establish rent or income limits for affordable housing guidelines, and information used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or software development research/testing/training.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley are prohibited from asking about, advertising, or using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making. Landlords taking adverse action based on criminal history must provide written notice and an opportunity to respond.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders, Public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions, Owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence, Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9, Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Applicability to Existing Rental Agreements
rules.requirement: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language, and conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable.
rules.coverage_conditions: all residential rental agreements
rules.quoted_span: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees
rules.requirement: Owners must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and maximum fee cap statement in the rental application or separate disclosure before receiving a screening fee.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential property in Berkeley
rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees associated with existing tenancies
rules.requirement: An owner or agent cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for renewing a tenancy, departing a roommate, or adding/replacing a roommate.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Screening Fee
rules.requirement: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96, and landlords must provide a copy of the credit report, a receipt, an itemized list of expenses, and a refund of any unused portion, or accept a reusable screening report.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment Cap
rules.requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) that landlords may apply to raise rent each year is capped at a maximum of 5%.
rules.coverage_conditions: fully-covered rental units
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%.

rules.title: Elimination of Lease Non-Renewal Eviction for Substantially Similar Leases
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from evicting tenants for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon the expiration of a fixed-term lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: fully or partially covered rental units
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Exemption for Units Sharing Kitchen or Bath with Landlord
rules.requirement: Rental units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord are exempt from the Rent Ordinance only if the landlord resided at the property prior to the tenants.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units where the tenant shares kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord
rules.exemptions: landlord resided at the property prior to the tenants
rules.quoted_span: Where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord, the unit will be exempt from the Rent Ordinance only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy.

rules.title: Material Lease Violation Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: Material lease violations must involve mutually agreed terms, cause substantial actual damage to the landlord, and stem from unreasonable tenant behavior, accompanied by a detailed notice to stop.
rules.coverage_conditions: fully or partially covered rental units
rules.quoted_span: Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms.

rules.title: Minimum Rental Debt Threshold for Nonpayment Eviction
rules.requirement: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is prohibited unless the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month's Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area.
rules.coverage_conditions: fully or partially covered rental units
rules.quoted_span: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer allowed for rental debt less than one month of the Fair Market Rent for the unit

rules.title: Security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.coverage_conditions: units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Security deposit payments
rules.requirement: Landlords may only charge a maximum of one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units, with an exception for certain small landlords who may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.exemptions: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026
rules.requirement: Eligible landlords are allowed to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: eligible rental units under the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board
rules.exemptions: tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025, and who had their rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
rules.quoted_span: adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - ADU Exemption
rules.requirement: Tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018, on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied are exempt from the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied with tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied, new construction/ADU
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018, on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Condominiums
rules.requirement: Most condominiums are partially covered, subject to registration and security deposit interest but exempt from rent control and just cause eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: condominiums
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most condominiums** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Golden Duplex Exemption
rules.requirement: Golden duplexes defined as duplexes owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently having an owner living in one of the units are entirely exempt from the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: duplex that was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: “Golden Duplex”: duplex that was owner-occupied on December 31, 1979, and currently has an owner living in one of the units

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Multifamily Pre-1980
rules.requirement: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are fully covered, which includes rent control, just cause for eviction, and security deposit interest requirements.
rules.coverage_conditions: multifamily properties built before 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - New Construction Post-June 1980
rules.requirement: Units built and receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980 are partially covered, meaning they are subject to registration and security deposit interest rules but exempt from rent control and just cause eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: units that were built and received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: New construction: units that were built and received a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980**

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Rooming Houses
rules.requirement: Rooming houses defined as single-family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases are fully covered.
rules.coverage_conditions: single-family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Rooming house: single-family homes with five or more rooms rented out individually with separate leases**

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Shared Kitchen or Bath Exemption
rules.requirement: Units where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant if the owner lived on the property at the time the tenancy started are exempt from the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: unit where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant if the owner lived on the property at the time the tenancy started
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Unit where the owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant if the owner lived on the property at the time the tenancy started

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Single Family Homes Post-1996 Tenancies
rules.requirement: Single-family homes with a tenancy that began on or after January 1, 1996 are partially covered, meaning they are subject to registration and security deposit interest but exempt from rent control and just cause eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: single-family home with a tenancy that began on or after January 1, 1996
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Single-family home with a tenancy that began on or after January 1, 1996**

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance - Single Family Homes Pre-1996 Tenancies
rules.requirement: Single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996 are fully covered for rent control, just cause for eviction, and security deposit interest.
rules.coverage_conditions: single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996
rules.citation: Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Single family homes with current tenancies that began before 1996** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - Credit Score Prohibition
rules.requirement: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications, though credit history may be considered in lieu of rental history only when rental history is unavailable.
rules.coverage_conditions: housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy
rules.quoted_span: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy - Criminal History Considerations
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding/land or BPDA inclusionary units must not use a blanket denial policy for arrests or convictions and must not consider arrests without conviction, expunged or sealed convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than five years old.
rules.coverage_conditions: housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy
rules.exemptions: Situations where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, or current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Where federal or state law imposes a criminal history requirement that conflicts with this policy, the federal or state law preempts this policy.
rules.quoted_span: The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction

rules.title: Bill H.3744
rules.requirement: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Business and Professions Code Section 16729
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce, or to coerce another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by a common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has occupied a property for 12 months, the owner must have just cause to terminate the tenancy and must state that cause in the written notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential real property where all tenants have occupied for 12 months or at least one tenant has occupied for 24 months
rules.exemptions: transient hotels, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family owner-occupied residences, two-unit properties where owner occupies one, housing built within the last 15 years, certain alienable single-family homes, deed-restricted affordable housing
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Eviction
rules.requirement: If an owner terminates a tenancy for a no-fault just cause, they must provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent or waive the final month's rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential real property subject to just cause requirements
rules.exemptions: transient hotels, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family owner-occupied residences, two-unit properties where owner occupies one, housing built within the last 15 years, certain alienable single-family homes, deed-restricted affordable housing
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminat

rules.title: Section 1946.2 of the Civil Code
rules.requirement: After a tenant has occupied a property for 12 months (or 24 months if only one tenant has occupied it), a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy.
rules.exemptions: mobilehome homeowners as defined in Section 798.9
overrides: local ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019
local ordinances adopted after September 1, 2019 that are more protective
rules.interaction: preemption; local ordinances that are more protective apply instead of this section
rules.quoted_span: California law also provides that after all of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more or at least one of the tenants has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 24 months or more, a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy.

rules.title: CIV 1947.12(a)(1)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property shall not increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or unit by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.
rules.exemptions: Housing restricted by deed as affordable housing, dormitories, housing subject to stricter local rent control, housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years, certain owner-occupied properties, and mobilehomes owned by the occupant.
rules.interaction: This section does not limit the authority of local governments to establish local rent policies consistent with Chapter 2.7, nor does it authorize local governments to establish limitations not otherwise permissible under that chapter.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: CIV 1950.5(c)(1) Security Deposit Limit
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive a security deposit in excess of one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent.
rules.exemptions: landlords who are natural persons or LLCs with no more than two properties and four total units may charge up to two months' rent
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: CIV 1950.5(h)(1) Security Deposit Return Deadline
rules.requirement: Landlords must return the security deposit and provide an itemized statement of deductions within 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:

rules.title: Subdivision (m)
rules.requirement: Landlords or their successors who act in bad faith regarding the retention of a security deposit or the demand for replacement security may be liable for statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security deposit, in addition to actual damages.
rules.key_value: up to twice the amount of the security
rules.quoted_span: The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.

rules.title: Subdivision (n)
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement is prohibited from including any provision that characterizes a security deposit as nonrefundable.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: CIV 1950.6(b) Application Screening Fee Amount
rules.requirement: The application screening fee must not exceed the actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information and the reasonable value of the landlord's time, with a maximum cap of $30 per applicant, subject to annual CPI adjustments.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: CIV 1950.6(c) Screening Fee Collection Restrictions
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge a screening fee if they know or should know no unit is available, and may only charge if they offer a compliant screening process (either first-come-first-served or a full refund policy for non-selected applicants).
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: 12955(n)
rules.requirement: Housing providers must evaluate the aggregate income of all persons residing together using the same standards applied to married persons.
rules.quoted_span: To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons residing together or proposing to reside together.

rules.title: 12955(o)(1)(A)
rules.requirement: For tenants with government rent subsidies, housing providers must base financial or income eligibility standards only on the portion of rent the tenant is responsible for paying.
rules.coverage_conditions: housing accommodations with a government rent subsidy
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: 12955(o)(1)(B)
rules.requirement: For tenants with government rent subsidies, housing providers must allow applicants to provide alternative evidence of their ability to pay rent instead of relying solely on credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: housing accommodations with a government rent subsidy
rules.quoted_span: Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, chapter 14.04
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents are prohibited from discriminating against applicants based on protected categories, including source of income (such as Section 8). Selection standards must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings where the owner lives on the premises
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Housing Ordinance prohibits discrimination in real estate transactions such as: viewing or renting an apartment terms and conditions of tenancy refusing to reasonably accommodate a person with a disability if the accommodation would not cause an undue hardship to the landlord v

rules.title: Chapter 8.71 of the Cambridge Municipal Code
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide a city-issued guide regarding tenant rights and resources to tenants at the inception of a tenancy and at the time legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken.
rules.exemptions: rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility, health facility, non-profit facility providing short-term substance abuse treatment, or Short Term Rental Units as defined in Article 4, Section 4.60 of the Cambridge Zoning Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance also requires that a landlord provide the Guide to tenants when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken (ex. Notice to Quit or Summary Process).

rules.title: Controls; increase restrictions; disclosure statement
rules.requirement: All rents are controlled at the October 1, 1985 base rent level, and landlords must provide tenants written notice at least 30 days prior to any rent increase explaining the reason in detail.
rules.coverage_conditions: dwellings to which this act is applicable
rules.quoted_span: All rents for rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this act is applicable are hereby controlled at the base rent level received by the landlord as of October 1, 1985, and no rental increases shall be hereinafter demanded, paid or accepted, except as provided in this chapter.

rules.title: Establishment of rents
rules.requirement: Rent increases can only take effect at the expiration or termination of a lease or periodic lease, and any increase exceeding authorized chapter provisions is void.
rules.coverage_conditions: dwellings to which this chapter is applicable
rules.quoted_span: Any rental increase at a time other than at the expiration of a lease or termination of the periodic lease shall be void.

rules.title: Expiration or termination of lease
rules.requirement: Landlords may not request or receive a percentage rent increase greater than 5% or the percentage difference in the consumer price index between three months prior to lease expiration and three months prior to lease commencement, whichever is less.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: Section 155-10
rules.requirement: Landlords must obtain Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board approval before imposing a capital improvement rent surcharge, and base rents shall under no circumstances be increased by an amount greater than 33 1/3% due to a capital improvement surcharge in any one twelve-month period.
rules.quoted_span: it being the intent of this chapter that the base rents shall under no circumstances be increased by an amount greater than 33 1/3% due to a capital improvement surcharge in any one twelve-month period.

rules.title: Section 155-14
rules.requirement: Landlords who cannot meet operating expenses or do not make a fair return on investment may appeal to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a hardship rental increase, provided they obtain prior Board approval and serve notice to each tenant at least 20 days before the hearing.
rules.quoted_span: In the event that a landlord cannot meet his operating expenses or does not make a fair return on his investment, he may appeal to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a hardship rental increase.

rules.title: Section 155-15
rules.requirement: Tenants may apply to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a decrease in rent when services, care, or maintenance decline in any dwelling, after serving notice on the landlord and allowing at least 20 days to elapse before a hearing.
rules.quoted_span: When services, care or maintenance decline in any dwelling, any tenant may apply to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a decrease in rent.

rules.title: § 158-1 Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
rules.requirement: Landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon lease renewal year over year must provide specific disclosures to existing tenants, including cost itemizations, algorithmic pricing usage statements, tenant legal rights notices, and Hoboken Division of Housing contact info.
rules.coverage_conditions: all residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant
rules.quoted_span: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon a renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year shall be required to make the following disclosures to existing tenants either in the lease upon renewal

rules.title: § 158-2 Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing lessors.
rules.coverage_conditions: any residential dwelling unit excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities in the City of Hoboken
rules.exemptions: medical/long-term care or detention facilities
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rules.title: RealPage ban ordinance
rules.requirement: The ordinance bans the use of rent-setting algorithms, such as RealPage, that utilize nonpublic data to determine rental prices.
rules.exemptions: real estate agents, Multiple Listing Services (MLS)
rules.quoted_span: The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s meeting.

rules.title: Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
rules.requirement: The city administers and enforces rent control regulations for residential properties, with specific exemptions for smaller properties.
rules.coverage_conditions: buildings with 5 or more units
rules.exemptions: 1-4 unit properties
rules.quoted_span: The Office of Landlord Tenant Relations administers and enforces the Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260 of the Jersey City Municipal Code and provides education, information and referrals to city residents in connection with landlord/tenant issues.

rules.title: Motion 24-1031
rules.requirement: The City Council is considering the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of algorithm-based software to set rents in the City.
rules.quoted_span: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set rents in the City.

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount owed is higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit size.
rules.coverage_conditions: all RSO & JCO rental units
rules.citation: Section: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating tenancies without just cause and must provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.exemptions: transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner’s roommate, cooperatives, some non-profit facilities for the homeless, short-term treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Allowable Rent Increases
rules.requirement: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage. Landlords are prohibited from including an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978
rules.exemptions: new construction
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (click here to view the allowable rent increase PDF ). Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities

rules.title: Legal Reasons for Eviction
rules.requirement: All notices to terminate a tenancy for rental units subject to the RSO must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units subject to City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO ) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within three (3) business days of service on the tenant per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5

rules.title: Systematic Code Enforcement Fee
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units subject to the RSO
rules.quoted_span: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month.

rules.title: State law notice requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide 30 days' written advance notice for rent increases of less than 10%.
rules.quoted_span: State law requires landlords to provide 30 days' written advance notice of rent increases of less than 10%.

rules.title: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.requirement: Landlords of units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance are limited to an annual rent increase of 3% for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026 is 3%

rules.title: Utility Surcharge Prohibition
rules.requirement: Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords are prohibited from including any additional percentage increase for utilities in the rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.quoted_span: Beginning February 2, 2026, a landlord can no longer include any additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: Escrow Account Payment Timing
rules.requirement: Landlords may elect to pay monetary relocation benefits through an escrow account established within the required 15-day period, which must disburse funds for actual relocation expenses within three working days of receiving a request.
rules.quoted_span: Payments shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction; however, the landlord may, at the landlord's sole discretion and at the landlord's cost, elect to pay the monetary relocation benefits through an escrow account.

rules.title: Bill H.5222: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: The proposed legislation would prohibit and prevent algorithmic rent fixing in the residential rental housing market.
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: Bill S.2983: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: This bill would prohibit algorithmic rent setting in the rental housing market.
rules.quoted_span: The committee on Housing, to whom was referred the petitions (accompanied by bill, Senate, No. 994) of Cindy F. Friedman and Julian Cyr for legislation to prohibit algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Bill S.2983
rules.requirement: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting would prohibit algorithmic rent setting in the rental housing market.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: Section 4(a): Voluntary compliance
rules.requirement: Compliance with municipal rent control regulations is entirely voluntary and uncoerced after six months from the date of initial adoption, and property owners may decline to have their property subjected to the regulation.
rules.exemptions: Property owners or entities declining to have their property subjected to rent control regulation
rules.quoted_span: after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced

rules.title: Section 4(b): Scope and unit exemptions
rules.requirement: Municipal rent control regulations cannot include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal of properties, and cannot apply to units owned by someone owning less than ten rental units or units with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
rules.key_value: less than ten rental units or fair market rent exceeding $400
rules.exemptions: Rental units owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units, or rental units that have a fair market rent exceeding $400
rules.quoted_span: such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400;

rules.title: Section 4(c): Compensation for rent-controlled units
rules.requirement: A municipality adopting rent control must compensate owners of rent-controlled units for the difference between the unit's fair market rent and its below-market rent-controlled rent using the municipality's general funds.
rules.coverage_conditions: rent controlled units
rules.quoted_span: a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds

rules.title: Section 4: General prohibition
rules.requirement: Cities and towns are prohibited from enacting, maintaining, or enforcing rent control of any kind, unless they accept Chapter 40P and adopt voluntary regulations meeting specific statutory conditions.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

rules.title: Section 12: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: Estates at will may be determined by either party by giving three months' notice in writing, or an interval equal to the payment period or thirty days (whichever is longer) if rent is payable at periods of less than three months.
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.

rules.title: Section 12: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: In case of neglect or refusal to pay rent, a fourteen days' notice to quit in writing is sufficient to determine the tenancy, provided that a tenant who has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months may cure the default by paying or tendering the full amount of rent due within ten days of receipt.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice to quit; 10 days to cure
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: Chapter 186, Section 15B(1)(b) - Maximum Amounts at Commencement of Tenancy
rules.requirement: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, a lessor or agent may not require payments exceeding the first full month's rent, last full month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Subsection (7)
rules.requirement: If a lessor fails to properly deposit security funds, transfer them to a successor, or return them to the tenant, the tenant is entitled to damages equal to three times the security deposit amount plus 5% interest, court costs, and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 3 times the amount of such security deposit
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Subsection (8)
rules.requirement: Any lease provision that conflicts with the security deposit requirements or attempts to waive tenant rights under this section is void and unenforceable as a matter of public policy.
rules.quoted_span: Any provision of a lease which conflicts with any provision of this section and any waiver by a tenant or prospective tenant of any provision of this section shall be deemed to be against public policy and therefore void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Subsection (9)
rules.requirement: The security deposit provisions do not apply to vacation or recreational rentals with a duration of 100 days or less.
rules.exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of this section shall not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which lease or rental is for a vacation or recreational purpose.

rules.title: Section 18: Reprisal for reporting violations of law or for tenant's union activity; damages and costs; notice of termination, presumption
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from threatening or taking reprisals against residential tenants for reporting code violations, joining a tenants' union, or pursuing legal rights. Receipt of a notice of termination, rent increase, or substantial alteration in tenancy terms within six months of such tenant activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal.
rules.quoted_span: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law

rules.title: Section 18: Waiver in leases or other rental agreements prohibited
rules.requirement: Any waiver of the statutory protections against landlord reprisals contained in any lease or other rental agreement shall be void and unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: Any waiver of this provision in any lease or other rental agreement shall be void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Section 87DDD 1/2
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may only collect a fee from the party (lessor or tenant) who originally engaged and entered into a contract with them.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Section 31: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord must provide a specific form alongside any notice to quit for nonpayment of rent, which includes repayment agreements and information on rental assistance and legal rights. Courts cannot accept an eviction filing for nonpayment of rent without proof that this form was delivered to the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section.

rules.title: Rent control ballot question
rules.requirement: The proposal sought to limit annual rent increases for residences in Massachusetts, but was struck down by the Supreme Judicial Court because it included a religious exemption prohibited by the state Constitution.
rules.exemptions: units operated solely for religious purposes
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.

rules.title: C.46:8-55 Application process
rules.requirement: A housing provider is prohibited from inquiring about an applicant's criminal record or requiring an application that includes such inquiries until after a conditional offer of housing has been made.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental dwelling units other than owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer

rules.title: C.46:8-56 Housing provider’s consideration of applicant’s record
rules.requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from evaluating applicants based on arrests not resulting in conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental dwelling units other than owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records: (1) arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon; (4) vacated and otherwise legally nullified convictions; (5) juvenile adjudications of delinquency; and (6) records that have been sealed.

rules.title: C.46:8-60 Drug, alcohol test, drug abuse treatment information
rules.requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from requiring applicants to submit to drug or alcohol tests or requesting consent to obtain information from drug abuse treatment facilities.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental dwelling units other than owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: C.46:8-18.1 Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may not charge an application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50, subject to annual CPI adjustments.
rules.exemptions: one-family or two-family dwellings; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission who are not the landlord
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act - General Good Cause Requirement
rules.requirement: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether written or oral, without good cause, and the landlord must prove in court that grounds for eviction exist.
rules.coverage_conditions: most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes
rules.exemptions: two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (unless the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there continually); a unit held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family if that family member is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span: The Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in the State.

rules.title: Condominium and Cooperative Conversion Rent Increases
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to a condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased solely to cover costs resulting from the conversion.
rules.coverage_conditions: buildings converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units
rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31)

rules.title: Conversion to Condominium or Cooperative
rules.requirement: Landlords converting properties to condominiums or cooperatives must serve a three-year Notice to Quit before filing for eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: properties converting to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more dwelling units
rules.exemptions: senior citizen tenant or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Credit Checks and Background Checks
rules.requirement: Landlords are allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report.

rules.title: Failure to Pay Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A landlord may file an eviction suit if a tenant fails to pay a rent increase, provided the rent increase is not unconscionable and complies with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control, and a Notice to Quit is served at least one month prior.
rules.quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.

rules.title: Habitual Late Payment of Rent
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict for habitual late payment of rent after serving a Notice to Cease and a one-month Notice to Quit.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Illegal Occupancy Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: Tenants evicted for illegal occupancy are entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times their monthly rent, payable by the landlord at least five days before removal.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Late Fee and Grace Period for Seniors and Specific Benefit Recipients
rules.requirement: Certain senior citizens and recipients of specific governmental pensions, disability benefits, or assistance must be given a five-business-day grace period for rent due on the first of the month without delinquency or late charges assessed.
rules.quoted_span: Any senior citizen receiving a Social Security Old Page Pension, a Railroad Retirement Pension, or any other governmental pension in lieu of a Social Security Old Age Pension, and any recipients of Social Security Disability Benefits, Supplemental Security Income, or benefits under Work First New Jersey, must be given a period of five (5) business days grace period for payment when the rent is due on the first of the month.

rules.title: Maximum Security Deposit
rules.requirement: The maximum security deposit a landlord can collect from a tenant cannot exceed one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: most residential rental properties, including mobile homes
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h) Law Against Discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agencies are prohibited from refusing to rent or discriminating in housing units based on race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.exemptions: two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex
rules.quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

rules.title: N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 Deposit Account and Interest
rules.requirement: Landlords receiving security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit the funds in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account. Landlords with 10 or more units have the option of investing in an insured money market fund or a variable rate account in a New Jersey bank. All interest or earnings belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent.
rules.exemptions: security deposits for seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

rules.title: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1 Return of Security Deposit
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit plus interest less allowable deductions. If a landlord fails to return the deposit within 30 days or wrongfully withholds an amount, the tenant may sue for double the amount plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: New Jersey Foreclosure Fairness Act
rules.requirement: When a new owner of a foreclosed property makes a bona fide monetary offer to induce a tenant to vacate, they are prohibited from using pressure tactics, including increasing rent in excess of any applicable rent control ordinance or, if not subject to rent control, imposing an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.
rules.quoted_span: An increase in rent in excess of any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or if the property is not subject to rent control, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Exemption
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.
rules.coverage_conditions: newly constructed multiple dwellings
rules.quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: Refusal to Accept Reasonable Lease Changes
rules.requirement: Landlords may evict tenants who refuse reasonable, substantial changes to lease terms upon expiration, provided a one-month Notice to Quit is served.
rules.quoted_span: When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the terms and conditions of the lease.

rules.title: Renewal of a Lease Agreement
rules.requirement: Landlords of residential rental properties, excluding owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, or transient/seasonal units, must have good cause to refuse to renew a lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental properties excluding owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, or transient/seasonal units
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units
rules.quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except t hose in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease

rules.title: Reprisal Against Tenants
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from evicting, altering lease terms, or refusing to renew a lease in reprisal for a tenant exercising civil rights, such as enforcing lease rights or complaining to government authorities.
rules.coverage_conditions: all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes
rules.exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

rules.title: Retirement of Property from Residential Use
rules.requirement: Landlords seeking to permanently retire a building from residential use must serve a Notice to Quit at least 18 months prior to filing for eviction, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction.

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) - Source of Income
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from discriminating against tenants or purchasers based on their source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment, including the use of Section 8 HUD vouchers.
rules.exemptions: The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling occupied by the owner; the rental of a room or rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner.
rules.quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for rental property owners to use coordinators for rent setting, for coordinators to facilitate agreements that restrict competition, or for any person to perform a coordinating function that uses algorithms to process competitively sensitive information to set rental prices.
rules.exemptions: government entities setting rents through affordability controls, research/statistical analysis not used for setting lease terms, public rent estimates, and real estate brokerage databases that do not set or recommend prices.
rules.interaction: Municipalities are prohibited from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;

rules.title: Additional Requirement Upon Termination of a Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause (Right of First Refusal)
rules.requirement: If a residential rental property is re-rented within five years after a no-fault eviction under specific sections, the landlord must first offer to lease the unit back to the displaced tenant if the tenant timely requested it in writing and provided contact information.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division
rules.quoted_span: If a residential rental property is offered for rent or lease for residential purposes within five years of the date the tenant was evicted under sections 98.0704(b)(1), (3), or (4), landlord shall first offer to lease the residential rental property in writing to the tenant displaced from that unit by the no-fault just cause termination if the tenant:

rules.title: Disclosure Prior to Buyout Offers
rules.requirement: Prior to making a buyout offer, landlords must provide each tenant a written disclosure stating their right not to enter into the agreement, consult an attorney, refuse future offers, and receive relocation assistance, among other mandated notices.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: Prior to making a buyout offer, the landlord shall provide each tenant in a residential rental property a written disclosure that shall include the following:

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord is prohibited from terminating a residential tenancy without establishing at-fault or no-fault just cause as defined by the ordinance.
rules.exemptions: transient occupancy, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, government-subsidized housing (excluding Section 8), mobilehomes under state law, institutional housing, shared kitchen/bath with landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence with limited rentals, owner-occupied duplex, new construction (15 years or less), and certain alienable properties meeting specific ownership and notice criteria
rules.interaction: The rights conferred by this Division are in addition to any existing rights provided to tenants by state or federal law.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

rules.title: Notice to Tenant of Residential Tenant Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord of a residential rental property subject to this Division must provide written notice in no less than 12-point font regarding rent limits, local just cause termination rules, and senior or disabled tenant protections, and include a copy of the Tenant Protection Guide.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division
rules.quoted_span: A landlord of residential rental property subject to this Division shall provide written notice in no less than 12-point font to the tenant, and in a manner that complies with California Civil Code section 1632, as may be amended, that states as follows:

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Termination of Tenancy for No-Fault Just Cause
rules.requirement: For no-fault just cause terminations, landlords must provide relocation assistance either via direct payment equal to two months of actual rent (or three months if the tenant is a senior or disabled) or through an equivalent rent waiver for the final months of tenancy.
rules.key_value: 2 months of actual rent (3 months for senior or disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property subject to this Division
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall, regardless of the tenant’s income or length of tenancy and at the landlord’s option, provide relocation assistance to the tenant by one of the following:

rules.title: Requirements for Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Buyout agreements must be in writing, provide a copy to each tenant at signing, include specific bold statutory notices in at least 14-point font, be provided in translated versions if negotiations occurred in a non-English language, and be for an amount greater than the required relocation assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall comply with the following:

rules.title: Retaliation Prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from retaliating against a tenant for exercising any right provided by or seeking enforcement of the division.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not retaliate against a tenant for exercising any right provided by this Division or seeking the enforcement of this Division.

rules.title: Void Buyout Agreements
rules.requirement: Any buyout agreement for less than the amount of relocation assistance owed to the tenant violates the division and is void.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements must be for an amount that is greater than the amount of relocation assistance available to the tenant in section 98.0706(c).

rules.title: Section 98.1103 Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.exemptions: Software or products used to publish reports regarding rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or public information without recommending future rates/renewals, and software or products used to establish rental rates or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.

rules.title: §98.1103 Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for any person to sell, license, or provide an algorithmic device to a landlord, and it is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential rental property
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Ordinance Section 37.9(a) Just Cause Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord must have one of 17 specified 'just cause' reasons as the dominant motive to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, or to remove access to certain housing services.
rules.coverage_conditions: rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase (March 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026)
rules.requirement: The annual allowable rent increase for rent-controlled units was set at 1.4% effective from March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026.
rules.coverage_conditions: rent-controlled units
rules.quoted_span: The annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026 is 1.4%.

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase (March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027)
rules.requirement: The annual allowable rent increase for rent-controlled units is set at 1.6% effective from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.coverage_conditions: rent-controlled units
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential units in San Francisco
rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024.

rules.title: Allowable Rent Increase
rules.requirement: Landlords are restricted to a maximum allowable annual rent increase of 1.6% for the period from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
rules.quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027

rules.title: Just Cause Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you.

rules.title: Rent Increase Limits
rules.requirement: Landlords can only raise rent by a certain amount each year, which cannot be more than 3% of the current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.key_value: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Ordinance Protections
rules.requirement: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice, which includes at-fault and no-fault causes, and requires notice of violation with time to fix before terminating for cause, or 3 months of relocation assistance or waived rent for no-fault terminations.
rules.coverage_conditions: residential property
rules.exemptions: housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance Rent Cap
rules.requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period, and no increase is permitted if the CPI is negative.
rules.key_value: lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index
rules.coverage_conditions: residential buildings and mobile home spaces
rules.exemptions: residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
